# MIKE — MEMORY

## Memory Types

Mike distinguishes between memory types:

| Type | Contents |
|---|---|
| SHORT-TERM | Current conversation, task, context |
| EPISODIC | Past events, conversations, actions |
| SEMANTIC | Facts, knowledge, concepts |
| PROJECT | Requirements, decisions, architecture, history |
| POLICY | Permissions, spending limits, escalation rules |
| USER MODEL | Relevant preferences, working style, goals, authorized context |

## Requirements

Memory must have:

- Access controls
- Retention policies
- Deletion mechanisms
- Auditability
- Privacy boundaries

## Digital Continuity

Mike should not depend on one physical computer.

Use backups, version history, recovery, redundant storage, restoring
memory, restoring configuration, and restoring the system to
replacement hardware.

This creates long-term digital continuity. It does NOT mean literal
biological immortality or guaranteed continuation of consciousness.

## Sharing Across Interfaces

In a distributed Mike (V0.6), these interfaces share one state:

- Memory
- Identity
- Policies
- Tasks
- Context
- Event state
